chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I heard him say: “Indeed, the hadd is not inherited as the diyah, wealth, and real property are inherited. Rather, whichever of the heirs undertakes it and demands it, then he is its wali. And whoever leaves it and does not demand it, then he has no right to it. That is like a man who falsely accuses a man, and the accused has two brothers: if one of them pardons him, the other may still demand it according to his right, because she is their mother altogether, and the pardon belongs to both of them altogether.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: financial compensation for injury or killing
key_terms.الْحَدَّ: the prescribed legal punishment being discussed in the case
key_terms.الْعَفْوُ: the act of pardoning or waiving the claim
key_terms.الْمَقْذُوفِ: the person who was subjected to the false accusation
key_terms.الْوَرَثَةِ: the heirs who may assert or leave the claim
key_terms.قَذَفَ: falsely accused of unlawful sexual conduct
key_terms.وَلِيُّهُ: the one entitled to act as claimant for that right

ai.seo_question: Is the right to demand the hadd for false accusation inherited like property or diyah?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the right connected to a hadd in a case of false accusation is not inherited in the same way as financial assets such as diyah, money, or property. Rather, any heir who actively claims the right may pursue it, while one who waives or neglects it loses his claim; the example given concerns brothers sharing a claim regarding slander against their mother.
